solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Nation state (7)

annotation.walkthrough: Read together, 'Nation state' is a single political term; split in two, each word defines a different Georgia.
annotation.definitionFit: Georgia is both a sovereign nation and one of the fifty US states.

entries.clue: Rot -- as may cooking ingredients? (2,2,3)

blocks.note: a slang phrase meaning to deteriorate, decay
literally, what raw ingredients do on their way into a cooking vessel

annotation.surface: Wondering whether ingredients left too long start to spoil.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical literal reading of the idiom, flagged by the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: To go to pot is to decay or fall into ruin, which is to rot.

entries.clue: Old vessel ripped apart by wave finally, a lot of water (5)

indicators.note: CAN is split open so E can sit inside it
take the last letter of wave

annotation.surface: An old boat broken up by a wave out at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old vessel' strongly suggests a ship, but the vessel is a humble CAN, and O is separate.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: the largest bodies of water on the planet are these.

entries.clue: Hit it off, not say vertically (3,2)

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upwards turns NOTEG round

annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit it off, not' looks like a warning against hitting something; 'not' belongs to the wordplay. NOT + EG written upwards spells GET ON.
annotation.definitionFit: Two people who hit it off get on well together.

entries.clue: Red coat, hideous style (3,4)

indicators.note: RED COAT made ugly, its letters deformed

annotation.surface: A fashion verdict on an ugly red coat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a fashion put-down, so 'style' reads as a verdict rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one particular decorative style of the 1920s and 30s.

entries.clue: Gear revolutionary with new galley (7)

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the crossword's standard revolutionary

annotation.surface: Kitting out a new ship's galley with fancy gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like an adjective praising the gear; it is a noun, Che.
annotation.definitionFit: A nautical sense: galley is the word sailors use for the room where food is cooked aboard ship.

entries.clue: Introduction to baron, king graciously admits, not so smooth? (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of baron
to admit is to let someone in, so NOBLY lets B enter its middle

blocks.note: to act nobly is to act graciously

annotation.surface: A king granting an audience to a baron, with a hint of roughness.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'not so smooth' is a loose way to say lumpy.
annotation.definitionFit: Something knobbly is covered in lumps, so not smooth.

entries.clue: Pilot fit for game (4,5)

blocks.note: a pilot study is a test

annotation.surface: An airman declared fit to play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' reads as a person who flies; here it is the trial run. A test match is an international cricket or rugby game.
annotation.definitionFit: A test match is an international game, most often in cricket.

entries.clue: Female embracing woman who's marrying a Scottish islander (9)

indicators.note: HEN wraps its arms round BRIDE and A

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird
the bride is the woman getting married

annotation.surface: A woman hugging her friend on her wedding day to a Scot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as marrying a Scotsman, but 'a' stays in the wordplay and the Scot is the definition. The Hebrides are islands off Scotland's west coast.
annotation.definitionFit: A Hebridean is a native of the Hebrides, Scottish islands.

entries.clue: County fair ultimately hosted by nobody? (7)

indicators.note: take the last letter of fair
NO FOLK holds R as a guest

annotation.surface: A county fair so poorly attended that nobody came.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose NO FOLK for nobody. Norfolk is an English county in East Anglia.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one English county, in East Anglia.

entries.clue: Score first of tries and win one mark in rugby (6-3)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the three words that follow: tries, win, one

blocks.clueFragment: first of tries and win one
blocks.note: the first letters of Tries, Win and One

annotation.surface: A rugby team scoring the first try and winning.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word sounds like a match report, so 'Score' reads as a verb; it is the noun twenty. The twenty-two is the line 22 metres from each try line.
annotation.definitionFit: In rugby the twenty-two is a line marked 22 metres from the goal line.

entries.clue: Thus live recording's beginning to get serious (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of recording

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist

annotation.surface: A live recording that starts to turn serious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Live recording' reads as a concert album; 'live' is the verb BE, pronounced to rhyme with give.
annotation.definitionFit: Sober means serious and solemn in manner.

entries.clue: Punishment of North American arrested by coppers (7)

indicators.note: NA is held inside PENCE, like a suspect in custody

annotation.surface: An American tourist arrested by the police and punished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' reads as police, which suits 'arrested'; here it means copper coins, British pennies.
annotation.definitionFit: Penance is punishment undergone to atone for wrongdoing.

entries.clue: Children's film absolutely not for child (7)

blocks.note: the Disney film about a young deer

annotation.surface: A parent ruling that a children's film is not suitable for a child.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a film certificate; BAMBI plus NO gives the Italian word for a baby, used in English.
annotation.definitionFit: Bambino is Italian for a baby or young child.

entries.clue: Irritable about one day giving evidence (9)

indicators.note: TESTY goes round I and MON

blocks.note: MON is the abbreviation for Monday

annotation.surface: A tetchy witness spending a day giving evidence.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a grumpy witness in court; that makes 'giving evidence' look like one phrase, but only 'evidence' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal synonym: what a witness states under oath counts as evidence.

entries.clue: Switch present in web-designing tool? (9)

indicators.note: switching round the letters of PRESENT IN

annotation.surface: A switch found in a website design program.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Web-designing tool' reads as software; the web is a spider's, and the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A spinneret is the organ a spider uses to spin its web.

entries.clue: Line and range wrong, mainly (2,7)

indicators.note: LINE and RANGE put together wrongly

annotation.surface: A marksman's complaint that both line and range were off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line and range' sounds like aiming a gun; the two words are simply mixed together.
annotation.definitionFit: In general means mainly, for the most part.

entries.clue: Attached to stern of boat, feeble tug (5)

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a boat, so take its last letter
WEAK is joined on after T

annotation.surface: A small tugboat roped to the back of a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tug' at the end looks like a tugboat in a nautical scene; it is a verb, a sharp pull.
annotation.definitionFit: To tweak something is to give it a sharp little tug.

entries.clue: Hold cold fish (5)

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
the ling is a sea fish of the cod family

annotation.surface: A fishmonger's instruction to keep the fish chilled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hold cold fish' reads as a storage instruction; 'Hold' is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gripping something tightly is holding it.

entries.clue: Persian perhaps accommodating naked form of entertainment (7)

indicators.note: CAT houses BARE inside it

blocks.note: a Persian is a breed of cat; 'perhaps' marks an example

annotation.surface: A Persian host putting up a nudist act.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Persian' reads as a person from Iran; it is the long-haired cat.
annotation.definitionFit: Cabaret is a form of entertainment of songs and sketches in a club.

entries.clue: Old coins, items in the distance? (9)

blocks.note: the farthing was a quarter of an old British penny
read as two words: distant objects

annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: read as FAR THINGS, the coin becomes objects far away. A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
annotation.definitionFit: Farthings were small British coins, withdrawn in 1960.

entries.clue: Where salmon might be farmed, is he feeding tiddler? (7)

indicators.note: IS HE goes into FRY, as food into a mouth

blocks.note: fry are young fish; a tiddler is a tiny fish

annotation.surface: A fish farmer asked whether he is feeding the small fry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feeding tiddler' fits the salmon farm so well that it reads as fish food; it is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A fishery is a place where fish such as salmon are bred or caught.

entries.clue: Tell on aristocrat (7)

annotation.surface: Informing on a nobleman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tell on' reads as a single phrasal verb, to snitch; only 'Tell' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: narrating the events of a story is telling it.

entries.clue: Gilbert & Sullivan initially aren't terribly funny (7)

indicators.note: take the first letters of Gilbert and Sullivan
GS and ARENT mixed up badly

blocks.note: the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan

annotation.surface: A critic's verdict that Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas aren't very funny.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terribly funny' reads as an intensifier; 'terribly' is the anagram instruction and 'funny' means odd, not comic.
annotation.definitionFit: Funny in the sense of peculiar means strange.

entries.clue: Fruit bats (7)

annotation.surface: Fruit bats, the animals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fruit bats' is a real animal, so it reads as one noun phrase; split, both halves define BANANAS, the second in its slang sense of mad.
annotation.definitionFit: Bananas are a fruit, and going bananas means going bats, crazy.

entries.clue: Assault gear (7)

blocks.note: to assault someone is to hit them hard
British slang for clothes or belongings

annotation.surface: Military kit for an attack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Assault gear' reads as army equipment. Clobber is British slang for clothes or kit.
annotation.definitionFit: Clobber means both to hit hard and, in British slang, one's gear.

entries.clue: Speak a little for a tenner (5)

indicators.note: only a small piece of the next words is used

annotation.surface: Offering to give a short talk for ten pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speak a little' reads as a request for a brief talk; 'a little' is the instruction to take part of what follows. A tenner is a ten-pound note.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a flavour of pomp: delivering a formal speech is speaking.

entries.clue: Saving one pound, still made up (5)

indicators.note: BUT keeps I and L safe inside it

blocks.note: L = pound, from the Latin libra

annotation.surface: Someone pleased at saving a pound on a purchase.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made up' suggests invented or cheerful; here it means constructed.
annotation.definitionFit: Something built has been made up, assembled from parts.

entries.clue: More unlikely to come up, looking back -- that's about right (5)

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so REAR is read from its end
about means surrounding, so RAER goes round R

blocks.note: to rear is to rise up

annotation.surface: Someone doubting a thing will crop up, looking back on it.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one hedging sentence; the definition stops at 'More unlikely'.
annotation.definitionFit: Rarer means less common, so more unlikely to happen.

entries.clue: Teaching a cutie, don distracted (9)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into confusion

annotation.surface: A university lecturer put off his tutorial by an attractive student.
annotation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, which ties the surface to 'Teaching' while the words are only letters to mix.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the whole business of schooling people is teaching.

entries.clue: Absolutely great in play (7)

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so TALL sits within TOY

blocks.note: to toy with something is to play

annotation.surface: Praise for an actor who was absolutely great in a play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great in play' reads as a review of a performance; 'play' is the verb TOY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are intensifiers meaning completely, without reservation.

entries.clue: Tear faked after the histrionics (7)

indicators.note: TEAR is made false, its letters rearranged
the anagram comes after THE

annotation.surface: An actor's crocodile tears after an emotional scene.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like the article attached to 'histrionics'; it is the first piece of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatre can mean exaggerated, dramatic behaviour, just like histrionics.
